verdict.rationale: Stagehand's core primitives take plain-English instructions: act() lets you write automation in plain English with no selectors, extract() takes an instruction plus an output shape, and observe() discovers actions from the page. The v3 agent turns high-level tasks into autonomous workflows, and the MCP integration controls browsers with commands like "click the login button". Community users corroborate that it generates actions dynamically and is resilient to DOM changes. Missing for 10: independent hands-on evidence of how reliably natural-language commands are interpreted, and v4 drops the autonomous loop, so multi-step orchestration falls back to user-written code.
